meta_title: NCERT Ex 8.1 Q2: Area Bounded by y²=9x, x=2 to 4
meta_desc: Solve NCERT Class 12 Ex 8.1 Q2: find the area bounded by y²=9x, the lines x=2, x=4 and the x-axis by integrating w.r.t. x, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Area Under y = 3√x Quiz (NCERT Ex 8.1 Q2)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding area by integration — reading the parabola, setting up the definite integral between x = 2 and x = 4, and evaluating it. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Area under a curve using definite integration (Application of Integrals)

questions.q: For the parabola y² = 9x, what is y in the first quadrant, written in terms of x?
questions.explanation: y² = 9x gives y = ±3√x. In the first quadrant y is positive, so y = 3√x.

questions.q: The area is measured against the x-axis between x = 2 and x = 4. Which definite integral gives it?
questions.explanation: Area under y = f(x) between the vertical lines x = a and x = b is ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx. Here f(x) = 3√x, a = 2, b = 4.
√x = x^(1/2). Raise the power by one to 3/2 and divide by 3/2, giving (2/3)x^(3/2) + C.

questions.q: In the first quadrant, the region under y = 3√x from x = 2 to x = 4 is bounded below by which line?
questions.explanation: The area is measured down to the x-axis, so the lower boundary is y = 0. The lines x = 2 and x = 4 form the left and right edges.

questions.q: Approximately, what is the value of the area 16 − 4√2 (in square units)?

faq.q: Why do we integrate with respect to x for this question?
faq.a: The bounding lines x = 2 and x = 4 are vertical, and the strip is measured down to the x-axis. Vertical strips of width dx and height y = 3√x make integration with respect to x the natural choice.

faq.q: How is y = 3√x obtained from y² = 9x?
faq.a: Taking the square root of both sides of y² = 9x gives y = ±3√x. Since the region lies in the first quadrant, y is positive, so we keep y = 3√x.

faq.q: What is the exact area of the region?
faq.a: The area equals ∫ from 2 to 4 of 3√x dx = 2x^(3/2) evaluated from 2 to 4 = 16 − 4√2 square units, which is about 10.34 square units.

faq.q: Would the answer change if we integrated with respect to y instead?
faq.a: The exact value stays the same, but the set-up is messier: you would express x = y²/9 and split the region across horizontal strips using the y-values at x = 2 and x = 4. Integrating in x is far cleaner here.
